turns.speaker: system
turns.text: I'm going to ask you some questions about how you and your family have been. I will ask about several areas. I will ask about how you've felt physically and your feelings. I will ask about school and friends. I will also ask about information about sleep or taking medicine. We will make a summary of your responses to share with your medical team. Your team is your doctors and your nurses. It is also other people who work with you here. I'll just call them your care team. The things you tell us help the care team to know how to help you. If you ever need to share something urgent or that can't wait, make sure you call your care team right away, or have your family help you call.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: I will start by asking about how you've felt physically. Have you had any problems with pain? What about sleep? What about nausea? What about your energy level?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I keep getting sores in my mouth after treatment days. I want to know why they keep coming back.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: I will make a note that you want to know why you keep getting mouth sores. Now I want to ask about your feelings. Have you felt sad, worried, grumpy, or lonely? Have you felt different from usual?

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: How is schoolwork going? Have you been able to stay in touch with your friends? How are those things going?

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: I will make a note that the mean kids at school are leaving you out. Have you had any difficulties with taking medicine, sleeping, eating, or using the bathroom regularly?

turns.speaker: user

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: Anything else that you would like to share?

turns.text: The night one is still the worst. It's hard to take the big white pill every time.

turns.text:
Okay, thanks for sharing all of that information. Now, I will make a summary of topics that may be helpful to discuss with your medical team. I'm going to give everything a number. 1. Why the mouth sores keep coming back
2. Mean kids at school
3. Hard to take the pill at bedtime
Which ones should we put on the top of the list?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: 3. The night pill.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text:
Here's your list:

2. Why the mouth sores keep coming back
3. Mean kids at school

turns.speaker: system
turns.text:
Thanks for talking with me today. I hope your conversation with the medical team will help. Please be sure to talk about these items in more detail with your medical team.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: I'm going to ask you some specific questions about how you and your family are doing. I will ask about problems in a number of areas. I will ask about your child's physical health, how you are doing emotionally, family and social things, practical things, and how things are communicated with you and your child. We will share a summary of your responses with the medical team. We hope that this process will help with communication and ensuring access to resources. The medical team is your doctors and your nurses. They can address things and offer referrals and support services as needed. This also gives us information about how these services may be working for you. Then we know what we may need to change. If you ever have urgent or time-sensitive concerns between visits, make sure that you call your care team directly.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, I'm ready.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: I will start by asking about how your child is doing physically. Have they had any problems with pain, sleep, appetite, or side effects of treatment?

turns.speaker: user

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: Got it, thank you. Anything else about that?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yes. He is hardly eating because of them. It hurts him to swallow, so he lives on smoothies and yogurt and he has dropped weight since the summer.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: Thank you for sharing that. I will add it to the list for further discussion with your medical team. Next, I would like to ask about how you and your family are doing emotionally. Are you noticing any problems with worry, sadness, anger or irritability? What about difficulty focusing? Or not feeling like yourself? Either for yourself or other family members.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We're all right. My mother being here helps more than she knows. I'm tired, but that's the job right now.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: Next, I would like to ask about family and social relationships. This is about you and your family. How are siblings doing? What about family conflict? What about social support from your family and community? Okay, how have family relationships and communication been? Any specific concerns?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The support side is where it's gone wrong for him. He's getting bullied at lunch and I've emailed his teacher twice about it. She says she'll keep an eye on it and nothing changes. Can we take him out of that school for the rest of the year? I don't want him walking back in there.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: Thank you for sharing that. I will add it to the list for further discussion with your medical team. Next, I would like to ask about day-to-day activities. These are the activities involved with managing your family and your child's treatment. Are you having any difficulty with finances? What about child-care? turns.text: Child-care is the piece that bends us, because it all lands at bedtime. Getting his chemo pill into him takes the better part of an hour. turns.speaker: system
turns.text: Thank you for sharing that. I will add it to the list for further discussion with your medical team.
